newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Italy says revised EMU plan ready soon.
newsitem.headline: Italy says revised EMU plan ready soon.

text.p: Italy's multiannual economic convergence plan to qualify for the European single currency is ready and will be forwarded to the European Commission in the next few weeks, an Italian spokesman said on Monday.

The plan, which updates budgetary stability efforts up to the year 2000, also addresses the much-needed reform of the state's social security system, the spokesman for Finance Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi told reporters.
But any details on the reform of state pensions would have to wait until September, he added. He was speaking in the margins of a regular meeting of EU finance ministers.

EU ministers are expected to adopt later on Monday recommendations to 10 EU countries, including Italy, found to run an excessive budget deficit in 1996 and urging them to put their financial house in order.

Ciampi's spokesman played down reports in the Italian press that the letter to Italy was particularly severe, saying that it also praised recent efforts to balance the books and took note of the upcoming new convergence plan.

The Commission last month predicted that Italy would record a budget deficit of 3.2 percent in 1997 and 3.9 percent in 1998, harming the country's chances of participating in the single currency -- the euro -- from the start in 1999. However, it admitted that the 1997 deficit could reach the three-percent target set in the Maastricht treaty on economic and monetary union.
